claims.text: The proposed predictive approach is a machine-learning model trained using transferable features derived from binary and ternary alloy data.
Features learned from binary and ternary alloys can capture local chemical and force-constant fluctuations in high-entropy alloys.
The ML approach will identify low-lattice-thermal-conductivity HEAs more accurately than current scattering models.
Conventional scattering models assume that greater multicomponent disorder produces greater force-constant variability and phonon attenuation.
The target materials are homogeneous, single-phase HEAs containing at least five randomly distributed elements, exemplified by FeCoCrMnNi.
High-entropy alloys exhibit inherent or severe lattice distortion.
Force-constant fluctuations in the target HEAs are approximately 20–50%.
Local chemical fluctuations and lattice distortions induce force-constant variations that enhance phonon scattering.
The important determinant of low thermal conductivity is how local environments modulate force constants, rather than merely the number of constituent elements.
Force-constant fluctuations reduce phonon lifetimes and lower lattice thermal conductivity.
An ML model using simpler-alloy features can accurately correlate force-constant fluctuations with reduced phonon lifetimes and thermal conductivity in HEAs.
The model will identify HEA compositions with lattice thermal conductivity near or below 10 W m−1 K−1.
FeCoCrMnNi has a phonon contribution to thermal conductivity of approximately 10 W m−1 K−1 or less and can serve as a benchmark.
Experimental observations show comparable phonon lattice thermal conductivities in FeCoCrMnNi and the binary alloy FeNi.
Acoustic-phonon attenuation in FeCoCrMnNi is stronger than in pure elements but of the same order as in binary alloys.
The approach is applicable only to single-phase, homogeneous HEAs with random elemental distributions.
The approach may fail for multiphase or segregated alloys because binary-system training data become non-transferable.
The quantitative accuracy improvement and reliability of extrapolation from binary or ternary alloys to HEAs are uncertain.
The hypothesis is falsified if measured lattice thermal conductivity differs from ML predictions by more than approximately 20% across multiple HEA compositions.
The hypothesis is falsified if the ML approach fails to improve predictive accuracy over conventional phonon-scattering models.
